newsitem.title: JORDAN: Two U.S. oil firms seek exploration deal in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. oil firms seek exploration deal in Jordan.

text.p: U.S. oil firms Huber Energy and Medallion Exploration are jointly negotiating with Jordan to explore in a 5,000 square km (1,900 square mile) area near the border with Saudi Arabia, an official said on Tuesday.
Khalid al-Shayab, director of Jordan's Natural Resources Authority, said he expected the two firms to clinch the accord to explore the concession in the Sarhan area next month.
Shayab told Reuters the U.S. firms had arrived at an initial agreeement on general principles of the terms of the deal with Jordan, including agreement on oil and gas production sharing.
But he declined to say how much money the companies would be committed to invest and how many exploration wells they would drill under the expected agreement.
Two other U.S. firms Anadarko Petroleum Corp and Trans Global Resources who signed production sharing accords last year were getting ready to develop their concessions, Shayab said.

Trans Global Resources has an eight-year concession to drill for oil the Dead Sea and Wadi Araba region. Jordan's deal with Anadarko commits the U.S. firm to spend $20 million in a 17,000 square km (6,600 square mile) area in the northeastern region.
Jordan does notnot produce oil in commercial quantities but produces 30 million cubic feet (850,000 cubic metres) of gas daily for electricity generation.
